The first stable release of Readme Studio. You design an animated, self-updating README in the browser, and a GitHub Action re-renders it on a schedule from your own repository. There's no server, no database and no third-party image host.

**[Open the studio](https://readme.niessen.dev/#/studio)** · [Presets](https://readme.niessen.dev/#/presets) · [Docs](https://readme.niessen.dev/#/docs)

```yaml
- uses: DavidNiessen/readme-studio@v1
```

## Highlights

### Studio
- A visual designer for **profile READMEs** (`<you>/<you>`) and **project READMEs** (any public repository).
- **18 presets**, 12 for profiles and 6 for projects (library, CLI tool, product launch, Python package, minimal, maintainer dashboard). You can also start blank.
- **54 widgets**: drag and drop, side-by-side rows, and an inspector for every option.
- **Theming**: 17 palettes or a palette generated from one accent colour, 12 embedded typefaces with real text metrics, radius, border, surface, texture and three motion levels.
- **Faithful preview**: GitHub's dark and light themes at desktop or phone width, with GitHub's own margins. Selecting a widget scrolls it into view.
- Undo/redo, keyboard shortcuts, a command palette, designs saved in your browser, share links, JSON editing and config import.
- **Export**: a ready-to-commit project (config, workflow, README, setup guide).
- Works on phones.

### Widgets
- **Profile**: hero banners, stats board, streaks, contribution graph, 3D skyline (GIF), coding rhythm, languages, trophies, timeline, top repositories, latest posts, local time and weather, and more.
- **Project**:
  - project hero, clickable shields and an install terminal;
  - code snippet, features grid and table of contents;
  - repository stats, vitals with CI status, star history, commit activity and a contributor wall;
  - npm/PyPI/crates.io downloads, a changelog from releases, a roadmap from milestones and a sponsor card.
- Every widget is hand-drawn SVG with CSS/SMIL animation, so it survives GitHub's sanitiser. Each one respects `prefers-reduced-motion` and renders in both colour schemes, served with `<picture>`.
- Markdown blocks keep real documentation searchable.

### Action
- `DavidNiessen/readme-studio@v1` (Node 24) fetches your data and renders every image. It force-pushes the images to an orphan asset branch and commits `README.md` only when the layout changed.
- **Data**: GraphQL with a token, or REST and the public contribution calendar without one. Optional `profile-token` for private counts. Weather from Open-Meteo, posts from any RSS/Atom feed.
- **Inputs**: `asset-branch`, `commit-readme`, `readme-path`, `output-dir`, `mock` and `dry-run`. Pull requests always render dry.

### For AI agents
- `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `widgets.json`, `presets.json` and `schema.json` on the site.
- A self-contained CLI: `node packages/engine/dist/cli.mjs`, with the commands `init`, `validate`, `build`, `link`, `widgets`, `presets`, `themes` and `schema`. `--json` gives machine-readable output.
- `#/studio?repo=owner/name` opens a committed config in the studio.
- The [`readme-studio` skill](https://github.com/DavidNiessen/skills): `npx skills add DavidNiessen/skills --skill readme-studio`.

### Project
- MIT licensed, with contributing guide, code of conduct, security policy, issue forms, Dependabot and CI on every pull request.
- **Releases**: every push to `main` publishes a pre-release. Full releases are cut by hand from **Actions → Release** and move the `v1` tag.

## Upgrading

Workflows exported from the studio already use `@v1`, so they pick up 1.x releases automatically.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/DavidNiessen/readme-studio/commits/v1.0.0
